P1: In January 2026 Roblox renamed about 46 yielding methods to use an Async suffix. Player:LoadCharacter is now LoadCharacterAsync, BadgeService:AwardBadge is AwardBadgeAsync and MarketplaceService:GetProductInfo is GetProductInfoAsync. Instance:WaitForChild and RemoteFunction:InvokeServer were not renamed and are still current. The old names still work the same way: they are marked deprecated for information only and no removal is scheduled. Use the Async names in new code.
P2: Set Workspace.AuthorityMode = Server (Workspace > Server Authority; fully released July 2026). It forces NextGenerationReplication, PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem, SignalBehavior = Deferred, StreamingEnabled and UseFixedSimulation. Put predicted gameplay logic in a function registered with RunService:BindToSimulation. That function must be deterministic and safe to re-run during rollback/resimulation. Read input from InputAction (not UserInputService) and sync state through attributes. Do not Destroy, reparent or EquipTool inside it. Use time() as the clock, not tick(), os.time() or os.clock().
P3: The property is Workspace.PlayerScriptsUseInputActionSystem. Phase 1 (June 2026) is opt-in and off by default. Phase 2 (early 2027, planned) turns it on by default. Phase 3 (mid 2027, planned) removes the property, so the new system becomes mandatory. Code at risk: anything that uses PlayerModule internals (for example require(PlayerModule):GetControls() and the control modules), code that relies on the old UserInputService/ContextActionService input sinking or priority behaviour, and forked or custom copies of the default PlayerScripts. Forks should set StarterPlayer.CreateDefaultPlayerModule appropriately and be migrated.
P4: October 2026 introduced platform-integrated chat, opted into with TextChatService.PlatformIntegratedChat = Enabled. When it is on, TextChatMessage.Text and Translation return an empty string with a warning, OnIncomingMessage and Player.Chatted give no message text, and custom chat UIs can no longer render messages; use the TextChannelWindow instead. Admin commands should move to TextChatCommand rather than parsing text. Timeline: opt-in testing until February 2027, on by default in February 2027, and mandatory around May 2027 (one announcement says March, so treat May as the hard deadline). Do not write new code that reads message text.
P5: Since July 2026 the limits are per experience, and in-game and Open Cloud requests share one budget per minute. The budgets are: Read = 300 + 40 x CCU, Write = 300 + 20 x CCU, List = 300 + 2 x CCU, Remove = 300 + 40 x CCU. Per key, write throughput is 4 MB/min (read 25 MB/min). Storage is 500 MB + 1 MB per lifetime player. UpdateAsync counts as one read plus one write. The old per-server limits still exist but are no longer the binding constraint. A bulk Open Cloud job can starve live servers, so throttle it yourself.
P6: Any paid random item counts, including indirect purchases. Crates bought with Gems count because Gems can be bought with Robux. Before purchase, show every possible outcome with numeric odds that sum to 100%. A long list can sit behind a clearly labelled Info/Details button, but not a bare icon, and rarity words alone are not enough. The Luck Potion changes probabilities, so before it is bought you must explain its numeric effect, and while it is active the displayed odds must show the player's real modified odds. Use the same table for the roll and the display. Per player, call PolicyService:GetPolicyInfoForPlayerAsync on the server and check ArePaidRandomItemsRestricted (and IsPaidItemTradingAllowed for trading). Fail closed if the call errors. For restricted players, hide or block the crates, or offer a non-random or direct-sale alternative. Re-check on the server in every purchase and trade handler, not only in the client UI.
P7: These are curated account tiers announced in April 2026 and rolled out in June 2026. Roblox Kids is for ages 5-8: it shows only Minimal or Mild content, and communication is off by default. Roblox Select is for ages 9-15 and allows content up to Moderate. To be available to them, a game must pass a selection evaluation, which looks at engagement by 16+ users, reports, the content rating and genre exclusions (social hangouts and free-form drawing are excluded by default). The game also needs a completed maturity questionnaire with an eligible rating (Minimal/Mild for Kids, up to Moderate for Select). The creator needs ID verification, 2-Step Verification, and an active Roblox Plus/Premium subscription or the publishing fee. Fees and thresholds change, so check the Audience Reach dashboard. Updates are re-evaluated as releases.
P8: Creator Rewards pays creators in Earned Robux, mainly based on engagement from Premium/paying users and on bringing in new or returning users who spend. Developer products and passes also give about 70% of the price as Earned Robux. DevEx converts Earned Robux to cash. The standard rate is 0.0038 USD per Earned Robux. Since 2026 there is a higher US 18+ rate of 0.0054 USD per qualifying Earned Robux. Legacy balances earned before September 5, 2025 still pay 0.0035 and are paid out first. You need at least 30,000 Earned Robux, must be 13 or older, and can make one request per month. Purchased Robux cannot be cashed out.
G1: Rules: there is one ProcessReceipt for the whole game, set in one server script; if two scripts assign it, one never gets receipts. Grant the item and save it inside the callback. Return PurchaseGranted only after the grant has been durably saved. Otherwise return NotProcessedYet, for example when the player has left, the profile is not loaded or the save failed, and Roblox will retry. Make it idempotent: record each PurchaseId in the player's own data in the same atomic save (UpdateAsync or a session-locked profile) as the grant, and skip the grant if the PurchaseId was already processed. Don't yield forever and don't error out. Charged but nothing received: PurchaseGranted was returned before or despite a failed save, the grant happened outside the handler, or it went into an unloaded profile. Received twice: there is no PurchaseId check, so retries grant again, or receipts are stored separately from the grant (or not atomically), so the item was saved but the receipt record was not.
G2: Use UpdateAsync whenever the new value depends on the old value or more than one server could write the key, which covers player data, currency, receipts and session locks. SetAsync blindly overwrites, and a GetAsync followed by SetAsync can lose updates. Transform function rules: it receives (oldValue, keyInfo) and returns (newValue, userIds, metadata). Return keyInfo:GetUserIds() and GetMetadata() as well, or they get cleared. Return nil to cancel the write. It must not yield. It can run several times when there is contention, so keep it pure: no granting items, firing remotes or other side effects inside it, only compute from the input. Handle oldValue == nil for new players. Wrap the call in pcall with retry and backoff. UpdateAsync costs one read plus one write.
G3:
Not safe. A NaN number passes typeof(gold) == 'number', and every comparison with NaN is false, so 'gold < 0 or gold > player.Gold.Value' never rejects it. createOffer then runs with NaN, which can corrupt balances or be used to dupe. The check also allows fractional values and 0. And the balance is only checked at offer time, not when the trade executes. Fix:
```lua
offer.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, gold)
  if typeof(gold) ~= 'number' or gold ~= gold or gold % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  if gold <= 0 or gold > player.Gold.Value then return end
  createOffer(player, gold)
end)
```
The NaN check is gold ~= gold, and the integer check also rejects ±inf. Rate-limit the remote too, and re-check and deduct atomically on the server when the trade completes.
G4: The Animator writes Motor6D.Transform every frame from the playing tracks, so anything you set in Heartbeat is overwritten on the next animation step. Write procedural offsets in RunService.PreSimulation (formerly Stepped). That runs after the animator has updated Transform and before physics and rendering, so combine your offset with the animated value: motor.Transform = motor.Transform * aimOffset for a local offset (or aimOffset * motor.Transform to re-aim the whole limb). Recompute the offset from scratch each frame and don't do Transform *= x cumulatively, or it compounds. The joint's world pose is Part0.CFrame * C0 * Transform * C1:Inverse(). Edit C0 only for a one-off or rest-pose change, such as re-seating the barrel or a permanent pose, not for per-frame aiming. C0 also replicates and isn't overridden by animation.
G5: Each joint is resolved separately by AnimationPriority: Core < Idle < Movement < Action < Action2 < Action3 < Action4. On any joint a track keys, the highest-priority playing track wins, and lower ones contribute only if the higher tracks' total weight is below 1. The default walk is Movement. If your swing is Core/Idle/Movement, it gets mixed with or overridden by the walk on the arm, so it looks weak. Set the swing's Priority to Action (or higher) before Play, in the animation editor or with track.Priority. Weights: tracks at the same priority blend by weight (two at weight 1 give 50/50). A high-priority track with weight 0.6 gives about a 60/40 mix with the layer below. Only joints the track actually keys compete, so an unkeyed arm keeps the walk. If the total weight is below 1 and nothing lies underneath, the joint drifts toward the rest pose. Fading weights (fadeTime, AdjustWeight) cross-blend the same way.
G6: It's a unit mismatch. Blender works in metres (1 unit = 1 m), and the FBX exporter's scale handling (unit scale or 'All Local' with a centimetre or 100x factor) gets read by Studio's importer as studs or centimetres, so the model ends up about 100x too big. Recommended: model at 1 Blender unit = 1 stud (check the size against a roughly 5-stud R15 avatar). In the FBX export use Apply Scalings: 'FBX Unit Scale' (or 'FBX All' with scale 1.0), apply all transforms first (Ctrl+A), Forward -Z / Up Y, and turn off Add Leaf Bones and animation simplify. In the importer, set the scale unit to Studs. Or export GLB, which avoids the FBX scale problem. Don't fix it by rescaling rigs in Studio.
G7: Modifiers are non-destructive and live only in Blender. The glTF/GLB exporter writes the base mesh unless 'Apply Modifiers' is enabled, and it's off by default. So Mirror leaves half the mesh, and the Bevel geometry and smoothing are missing. The fix is to turn on Apply Modifiers in the exporter's Data/Mesh settings, or apply them manually before export. The catch: on a rigged or skinned mesh, Apply Modifiers also applies the Armature modifier and modifier stack ordering, which breaks the rig and skinning, or the export drops shape keys. For rigged meshes, manually apply Mirror and Bevel (above the Armature) and keep the Armature modifier live. Also apply transforms, limit to 4 bone influences, and check face normals and shading after Bevel.
G8: 1) Stretching: fromScale(0.3, 0.3) is 30% of the screen width and 30% of the screen height, and screens have different aspect ratios, so the frame becomes a different shape on each device. Fix it with a UIAspectRatioConstraint (AspectRatio = 1 or your design ratio), or size one axis with SizeConstraint = RelativeXX/RelativeYY. Add UISizeConstraint or UITextSizeConstraint for limits if needed. 2) The hidden button: by default the ScreenGui may extend into the device unsafe area or under the Roblox top bar. Set ScreenGui.ScreenInsets = Enum.ScreenInsets.CoreUISafeInsets (DeviceSafeInsets avoids only the notch; CoreUISafeInsets also avoids the top bar), and SafeAreaCompatibility = None for new GUIs. Keep ClipToDeviceSafeArea on and don't hard-code a top-bar offset (or IgnoreGuiInset hacks). Only full-bleed decorative backgrounds should use ScreenInsets = None.

```lua
local RS = game:GetService('ReplicatedStorage')
local Items = require(game.ServerStorage.ItemCatalog) -- [id] = {price=, maxQty=}
local BuyItem = RS.Remotes.BuyItem
local last = {}

BuyItem.OnServerEvent:Connect(function(player, itemId, quantity)
  local now = os.clock()
  if last[player] and now - last[player] < 0.25 then return end
  last[player] = now
  if typeof(itemId) ~= 'string' or #itemId > 50 then return end
  if typeof(quantity) ~= 'number' or quantity ~= quantity or quantity % 1 ~= 0 then return end
  local item = Items[itemId]
  if not item or quantity < 1 or quantity > (item.maxQty or 99) then return end
  local coins = player:FindFirstChild('leaderstats') and player.leaderstats:FindFirstChild('Coins')
  if not coins then return end
  local cost = item.price * quantity -- price from server catalog, never client
  if coins.Value < cost then return end
  coins.Value -= cost
  Inventory.Add(player, itemId, quantity) -- server-side data
end)
game.Players.PlayerRemoving:Connect(function(p) last[p] = nil end)
```
The server owns the prices and the balance, validates type, NaN, integer and range, rate-limits, and cleans up the per-player table. The client only sends a request.
T2:
```lua
-- key 'player_'..userId stores {data=..., lock={jobId=, token=, time=}, receipts={}}
local LEASE = 90
function load(player)
  local token = HttpService:GenerateGUID(false)
  for attempt = 1, 5 do
    local ok, result = pcall(store.UpdateAsync, store, key, function(old)
      old = old or {data = defaultData(), receipts = {}}
      local l = old.lock
      if l and l.token ~= token and os.time() - l.time < LEASE then return nil end -- locked by another server
      old.lock = {jobId = game.JobId, token = token, time = os.time()}
      return old
    end)
    if ok and result and result.lock.token == token then sessions[player] = {data = result.data, token = token}; return end
    task.wait(2 ^ attempt) -- backoff, other server should release
  end
  player:Kick('Data busy, rejoin')
end
function save(player, release)
  local s = sessions[player]
  store:UpdateAsync(key, function(old)
    if not old or not old.lock or old.lock.token ~= s.token then return nil end -- lost lease: never write
    old.data = s.data
    old.lock = (not release) and {jobId = game.JobId, token = s.token, time = os.time()} or nil
    return old
  end)
end
```
Autosave every 30-60 s (shorter than the lease) renews the lock. PlayerRemoving does save(player, true). BindToClose saves everyone in parallel. Before teleporting, save and release the lock. The destination waits for the lock or retries. Grant items and receipts only in the same locked write.

T4: FireServer automatically passes the sending player as the first argument to OnServerEvent. The client also passed LocalPlayer, so on the server the arguments are (player, LocalPlayer, 50) and 'amount' is the Player instance, which causes the arithmetic error. Fix: don't pass the player on the client, use remote:FireServer(50). The server stays function(player, amount). Also validate amount on the server (typeof number, not NaN, within range), and never trust a client-sent player identity.
T5:
It's a race condition. In Studio solo playtests the local player often joins before your server Script runs and connects PlayerAdded, so the event has already fired for that player and your handler never runs. Live servers start scripts before anyone joins. The standard fix is to put the setup in a function, connect it, and then loop over the players already present:
```lua
local Players = game:GetService('Players')
local function onPlayerAdded(player)
  local ls = Instance.new('Folder'); ls.Name = 'leaderstats'
  local c = Instance.new('IntValue'); c.Name = 'Coins'; c.Parent = ls
  ls.Parent = player
end
Players.PlayerAdded:Connect(onPlayerAdded)
for _, p in Players:GetPlayers() do task.spawn(onPlayerAdded, p) end
```
Also avoid yields (like a DataStore load) before the connection is made.

local BadgeService = game:GetService('BadgeService')
local BADGE_ID = 123456

local function awardFinishBadge(player: Player)
  local ok, has = pcall(BadgeService.UserHasBadgeAsync, BadgeService, player.UserId, BADGE_ID)
  if ok and has then return true end
  for attempt = 1, 3 do

    task.wait(2 ^ attempt)
  end
  return false

T8: RenderFidelity is probably being overridden. When Workspace.MeshStreamingAndImprovedLoDs (mesh streaming and cloud-generated LoDs) is Enabled, the engine picks the mesh LoD itself and ignores the per-part RenderFidelity, so Precise does nothing and meshes still switch to lower detail at distance. The client device's graphics quality level and streaming also lower detail regardless. Fixes: check that Workspace property first. Keep important meshes within a sensible triangle budget at the source, so the generated LoDs look fine. For hero models use Model LevelOfDetail/ModelStreamingMode (for example Persistent or Atomic) where appropriate. Don't put Precise on everything: Automatic is the recommended default, and Precise everywhere hurts performance.
